meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'okay', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я пойду принесу выпить, окей?
examples.trans: I will go grab us something to drink, okay?

examples.text: Я уже всё решил. Одну треть на кладбище, две трети над океаном.
examples.trans: I've already sorted it all out. One third goes to the cemetery, two thirds over the ocean.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, back then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry', paired with 'забеспокоиться'.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'мекать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hint, imply'.

examples.text: На кого ты сейчас намекаешь, майор?
examples.trans: Who are you hinting at right now, Major?

examples.text: А я ни на кого не намекаю.
examples.trans: And I am not hinting at anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What do you mean? Where is Mishkin?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'волноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get nervous, worked up'.

related.gloss: not to to get nervous (negated infinitive)

examples.text: А что это ты так разволновался?
examples.trans: Why are you getting so worked up all of a sudden?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет разволноваться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to get nervous without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.
Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'shrimp, prawn' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'arugula, rocket' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The kitchen has run out of fresh arugula.

examples.text: Лёва, быстро принесите руколу со склада!
examples.trans: Lyova, quickly bring arugula from the storeroom!

examples.text: Где же лежит эта чёртова рукола?
examples.trans: Where is this damn arugula lying?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'завчера').

examples.trans: You were sitting right here the day before yesterday!
He arrived the day before yesterday.

examples.text: Ты же позавчера здесь сидела! Ты коньяк французский пила со мной!
examples.trans: You were sitting right here the day before yesterday! You were drinking French cognac with me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!
